tagline: A Baltic port with a thousand-year history, Gdańsk has a rebuilt Hanseatic old town, amber shops on Mariacka Street and the shipyard where Solidarity began.
overview: Gdańsk sits at the mouth of the Vistula on the Baltic Sea and was one of the richest members of the Hanseatic League. Merchants from across Europe built the tall, decorated townhouses on the Royal Way, which runs from the Golden Gate along Long Street to Long Market and the Neptune Fountain.

World War II began here at Westerplatte in 1939, and the old town was badly damaged, then carefully rebuilt. The riverside Long Embankment is lined with cafés and the medieval wooden crane, and Mariacka Street is famous for amber jewellery. St Mary's is one of the largest brick churches in the world.

In 1980, strikes at the Gdańsk Shipyard led to Solidarity, the movement that helped end communism in Eastern Europe; the European Solidarity Centre tells that story. Gdańsk forms the Tricity with the seaside resort of Sopot and the port of Gdynia.
